title: In Vivo Proton MRS
summary: 1H MRS reads a 0.2 to 4.5 ppm window that is only about 550 Hz wide at 3 T, sitting on top of a tissue water signal three to four orders of magnitude larger. Everything hard about the method follows from that: water and lipid suppression, shim quality, and chemical shift displacement set what you can measure long before SNR does. Concentrations of the reliably detected metabolites run from about 16 mM down to 1 mM, so a 5 minute single voxel acquisition needs roughly 8 cm3 of tissue at 1.5 and 3 T. Going to 7 T buys dispersion and SNR, which separates Glu from Gln and lets 15 or more metabolites be quantified, but it shortens every metabolite T2, worsens chemical shift displacement, and raises the achievable linewidth floor.

facts.label: Larmor frequency and spectral dispersion
facts.value: 42.577 MHz/T, so 63.9 MHz at 1.5 T, 127.7 MHz at 3 T, 298.0 MHz at 7 T; 1 ppm is 63.9, 127.7 and 298.0 Hz respectively
facts.note: The whole metabolite range from 0.2 to 4.5 ppm spans only about 550 Hz at 3 T, which is why linewidth and not SNR is usually the binding constraint.

facts.label: Principal chemical shifts
facts.value: NAA CH3 2.01 ppm; NAAG 2.04 ppm; tCr CH3 3.03 ppm and CH2 3.91 ppm; tCho N(CH3)3 3.20 ppm; mI 3.52, 3.61 and 4.05 ppm; Glu H4 2.35 ppm and H2 3.75 ppm; Gln H4 2.45 ppm; GABA 1.89, 2.28 and 3.01 ppm; GSH cysteine beta 2.95 ppm; Lac CH3 doublet 1.31 ppm with 3J = 6.9 Hz; lipid CH2 1.3 ppm and CH3 0.9 ppm; water 4.68 ppm
facts.note: tCr at 3.03 and tCho at 3.20 ppm are only about 22 Hz apart at 3 T and about 51 Hz at 7 T, so tCho quantification is a direct hostage to linewidth.

facts.label: Metabolite concentrations, healthy human brain
facts.value: tNAA 8 to 16 mM, tCr 6 to 10 mM, tCho 1 to 2.5 mM, mI 4 to 9 mM, Glu 6 to 12.5 mM, Gln 3 to 6 mM, GSH 1.5 to 3 mM, GABA 1 to 2 mM, NAAG 0.6 to 2.7 mM, Lac below 1 mM; lipid essentially zero in healthy parenchyma
facts.note: These are literature ranges, not point values; they span gray and white matter, region, age and quantification convention, and are quoted variously as mM or mmol per kg wet weight.

facts.label: Water concentration and the suppression target
facts.value: Brain tissue is 70 to 85 percent water by mass, which is 39 to 47 M, of which about 36 to 43 M is MR visible; MR visible water density taken as 0.78 in gray matter, 0.65 in white matter, 0.97 in CSF. VAPOR reduces residual water about 8-fold relative to a three pulse CHESS train
facts.note: Consensus sets the goal as residual water no taller than the largest metabolite peak, in phase and at a single frequency, rather than a fixed suppression factor.

facts.label: Lipid suppression factors
facts.value: Whole slice outer volume suppression gives 15 to 25-fold mean extracranial lipid suppression; dedicated adiabatic dual band schemes exceed 100-fold. Inversion recovery lipid nulling costs about 30 percent of metabolite signal at 3 T and 50 percent or more at 7 T
facts.note: 15 to 20-fold is usually enough for most MRSI voxel positions; the cost of IR is paid in metabolite T1 weighting that can differ between pathological and control tissue.

facts.label: Metabolite T2 at 3 T
facts.value: NAA CH3 247 +/- 13 ms in motor cortex and 301 +/- 18 ms in occipital white matter; tCr CH3 162 +/- 16 ms and 178 +/- 9 ms in the same regions; basal ganglia shorter for all metabolites. Across gray and white matter the full metabolite set spans 116 to 295 ms
facts.note: Regional T2 variation of NAA at 3 T is large enough that a single assumed T2 biases long TE quantification by tens of percent.

facts.label: Metabolite T2 at 7 T
facts.value: NAA CH3 130 to 191 ms, tCr CH3 90 to 131 ms (95 +/- 3 ms in occipital lobe), tCho 121 to 200 ms, mI 80 to 130 ms, across occipital lobe, motor cortex, basal ganglia and cerebellum. At 9.4 T all metabolite T2 values fall below 100 ms
facts.note: J-coupled metabolite T2 values are generally shorter than the singlets, and the NAA aspartyl multiplet decays faster than the 2.01 ppm methyl, so the two moieties cannot share one T2.

facts.label: Metabolite T1
facts.value: At 3 T, 0.97 to 1.47 s in gray matter and 0.87 to 1.35 s in white matter across NAA, Glu, tCr, tCho and mI; essentially unchanged from 1.5 T. At 7 T, T1 of tCr CH3 and NAA lengthen significantly relative to 3 T while tCho is similar
facts.note: T1 is the weakly field dependent quantity and T2 is the strongly field dependent one; the TR penalty at 7 T comes mainly from the longer tCr and NAA T1.

facts.label: Water relaxation used for quantification at 7 T
facts.value: T1 2130 ms gray matter, 1220 ms white matter, 4425 ms CSF; T2 50 ms gray matter, 55 ms white matter, 141 ms CSF
facts.note: Water referenced quantification needs these plus the voxel tissue fractions; a CSF fraction error propagates directly into every reported concentration.

facts.label: Achievable linewidth versus field
facts.value: The minimum achievable tCr 3.03 ppm linewidth rises linearly with B0 at about 1.35 Hz/T from 1.5 T to 9.4 T, reaching about 12.5 Hz at 9.4 T. Measured 7 T water FWHM is 11 to 14 Hz in occipital lobe, motor cortex and cerebellum, and 21 +/- 4 Hz in basal ganglia
facts.note: At high field the floor is set by B0 microsusceptibility within the voxel, not by shim hardware, so buying more shim channels does not recover it.

facts.label: Chemical shift displacement limits
facts.value: Consensus caps CSD at 4 percent per ppm for SVS and 2 percent per ppm for MRSI. A 3 T body transmit coil with B1max of 15 to 30 uT limits a conventional 180 degree refocusing pulse to about 1 kHz bandwidth; a typical 2D PRESS MRSI at 3 T then exceeds 10 percent per ppm, displacing the tCho box from the tNAA box by 1.2 cm in a 10 x 10 x 1 cm slab
facts.note: sLASER adiabatic full passage pulses run at roughly 4 to 6 kHz bandwidth, which is why sLASER and not PRESS is recommended at 3 T and above.

facts.label: SVS voxel size, TR, TE and scan time
facts.value: 8 cm3 (2 x 2 x 2 cm) in 5 min gives high quality spectra at 1.5 and 3 T; 4 cm3 in 5 min at 3 T still supports quantification beyond tNAA, tCr and tCho given a good shim. Recommended TR 1.5 s at 1.5 T and 2.0 s at 3 T. Shortest TE about 20 ms for STEAM and 30 ms for PRESS at clinical field, down to 6 ms for STEAM and SPECIAL at 7 T
facts.note: GSH and clean Glu from Gln separation need volumes larger than 8 cm3 or longer scans; going from a 20 mm cube to a 15 mm cube cuts the volume to 42 percent, so at equal averages you keep 42 percent of the SNR, and it takes roughly six times the averages to get back to where you were.

facts.label: MRSI resolution and scan time
facts.value: A 16 x 16 2D grid at about 1.5 cm3 nominal voxel takes roughly 5 min at TR 1500 ms with one average per phase encode and elliptical k-space sampling. A full 16 x 16 x 8 3D matrix at TR 1500 ms is over 51 min; elliptical or spherical sampling cuts 25 percent from 2D and 50 percent from 3D. Whole brain 3D EPSI at 3 T has reached 18 min at TE 20 ms
facts.note: Whole brain 3D MRSI with first and second order shims alone can leave up to 35 percent of voxels unusable at 3 T.

facts.label: MEGA-PRESS GABA editing
facts.value: Editing pulse on at 1.9 ppm, off at 7.5 ppm, TE 68 ms, TR 2000 ms, 256 transients from a 27 mL voxel, about 8.5 min. Theoretical J-difference editing efficiency is 50 percent for GABA (AX2) versus 100 percent for lactate (AX3). At 3 T and below, macromolecules contribute more than 50 percent of the 3 ppm edited signal, hence GABA+
facts.note: Symmetric MM suppressed editing (on 1.9 ppm, off 1.5 ppm, symmetric about the 1.7 ppm MM) removes most of the MM but makes the measurement far more sensitive to frequency drift.

practice: Shim with second order terms for SVS at 3 T and above; first order alone is only adequate at 1.5 T. Use FASTMAP or FAST(EST)MAP style projection shimming or a 3D field map, and report the achieved water FWHM in Hz with every dataset.

Acquire and store single transients, then frequency and phase align them before averaging and discard the corrupted ones. This is mandatory for J-difference editing and worth doing for every SVS acquisition.

Always acquire a water unsuppressed reference from the same voxel with the transmit frequency on water. Allow at least 9 s without RF excitation beforehand so T1 saturation loss stays under 10 percent even in cystic or CSF-rich voxels, and use it for eddy current lineshape correction as well as scaling.

Run editing and other frequency sensitive acquisitions before high gradient duty cycle scans such as DTI or long EPI. A heavy gradient session can drive frequency drift up to 5 Hz/min and it persists for 30 min or more.
Acquire editing data in 2 to 5 min blocks with an interleaved frequency adjustment between blocks, sized so that drift within a block stays at or below 5 Hz.

Prefer sLASER over PRESS at 3 T and above for both SVS and MRSI pre-localization; place the voxel away from air and tissue interfaces and away from the scalp, and add outer volume suppression to shape the excited region to the anatomy.
Use TE 144 ms when you need lactate inverted and separated from lipid, since 1/J is 144 ms for the 6.9 Hz lactate doublet; use the shortest achievable TE when you want mI, Glu, Gln and GSH.

Report the MRSinMRS minimum reporting set: field, sequence, TR, TE, voxel size and position, number of transients, water suppression method, shim method and achieved linewidth, analysis software and basis set, and the relaxation and tissue fraction corrections applied.
pitfalls: Reporting everything as a ratio to tCr hides changes in tCr itself. Creatine is not a stable internal reference in tumor, stroke, or creatine deficiency syndromes, and a falling denominator reads as a rising numerator.

Using a CRLB threshold as an exclusion criterion truncates the low concentration tail of the distribution and biases the group mean upward, because low true concentrations produce high CRLB. This bites hardest for GABA, GSH, Gln and Lac.

GABA+ conflates GABA with macromolecules that are over half the edited 3 ppm signal at 3 T. A GABA+ difference between groups can be an MM difference, or simply a difference in frequency drift or motion that changed the proportion of MM co-edited.

Chemical shift displacement splits a J-coupled spin system so that coupling partners sit in sub-volumes seeing zero, one or two refocusing pulses. The result is not just a shifted box, it is altered coupling evolution and reduced editing efficiency, and it is why MEGA-PRESS becomes unacceptable above 3 T without a dedicated local transmit coil.

The MRSI point spread function puts signal from outside the nominal voxel into it with both positive and negative sign. Subcutaneous lipid bleeds into voxels far from the scalp, so edge voxels must be excluded and the residual water and lipid maps inspected, not just the metabolite maps.

Long water suppression pulse trains such as VAPOR deposit magnetization transfer on the macromolecule pool and can bias metabolite amplitudes. Where this matters, metabolite cycling avoids the issue by not suppressing water at all.
